name: Ueli Steck
milestone_by_age_26: At age 18, climbed the North Face of the Eiger, one of the most notorious big-wall routes in the Alps; by age 25 had established new routes on Pumori in Nepal and a phenomenal mixed line on Mt. Dickey in Alaska.
early_history_summary: Started climbing at age 12 when a friend of his father took him to a local mountain in the Emmental valley. Quickly excelled, joining the junior national climbing team. By 17, achieved the 9th difficulty rating (UIAA) in climbing. At 18, climbed the Eiger North Face and the Bonatti Pillar in the Mont Blanc massif.
family_context_summary: Born as the third son to a coppersmith in Langnau im Emmental, a rural Swiss town. His father encouraged him to pursue whatever he chose '100 percent.' His two older brothers played competitive hockey.
primary_early_advantage_tags: alpine environment, early climbing, mentor guidance, junior national team
evidence_summary: Ueli Steck grew up in Langnau im Emmental, rural Switzerland, with the Eiger visible from his family home. He started climbing at 12, was mentored by veteran Himalayan guide Kari Kolber, and joined the junior national climbing team. By 17 he achieved 9th UIAA difficulty rating, and at 18 climbed the Eiger North Face. His father, a coppersmith, encouraged him to pursue climbing '100 percent.' The Swiss Alpine environment provided unparalleled proximity to world-class climbing objectives.
starting_point: Born to a coppersmith's family in Langnau im Emmental, rural Switzerland; third of three sons, father a coppersmith, mother Lisabeth.
current_position: Died on 30 April 2017 at age 40 in a fall on Nuptse, Nepal, while preparing for an Everest-Lhotse traverse; final status: one of the world's greatest alpinists, two-time Piolet d'Or winner.

trajectory.event: Climbed the North Face of the Eiger for the first time, establishing a lifelong relationship with the mountain.
Established new routes on the Eiger and Pumori in Nepal.
Climbed the Eiger, Monch, and Jungfrau within 25 hours with Stephan Siegrist.
Set first speed record on the North Face of the Eiger at 3 hours 54 minutes.
Won first Piolet d'Or for alpine-style ascent of Tengkampoche north face.
Soloed the South Face of Annapurna in 28 hours, winning his second Piolet d'Or.
Climbed all 82 4000m peaks in the Alps in 62 days; set new Eiger North Face speed record of 2h22m50s.
Died in a fall on Nuptse, Nepal, while acclimatizing for an Everest-Lhotse traverse.

name: Catharina Lodders
milestone_by_age_26: Crowned Miss World 1962 at age 20, becoming the second Dutch woman to win the title.
early_history_summary: Born in Haarlem, Netherlands. Won Miss Holland in May 1962, which qualified her for international pageants. Placed 3rd runner-up at Miss International 1962, then won Miss Benelux and Miss World 1962 in London in November.
family_context_summary: Born in Haarlem, Netherlands. Not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Catharina Lodders was born in Haarlem, Netherlands, and won Miss Holland in May 1962, which propelled her to international pageants. She won Miss World 1962 in London at age 20. Little is documented about her family background or early life before the pageants. Her physical appearance was the primary factor in her success.
starting_point: Born in Haarlem, Netherlands; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Married to singer Chubby Checker since 1964; lives in the United States; former model and corporate manager, now a grandmother.

trajectory.event: Crowned Miss World 1962 in London, the second Dutch woman to win the title.
Accepted marriage proposal of American singer Chubby Checker.
Married Chubby Checker; settled in Pennsylvania.
First child, Bianca Johanna Evans, born in Philadelphia.

name: Saroj Khan
milestone_by_age_26: Choreographed her first Bollywood song at age 14, and became an independent film choreographer with Geeta Mera Naam (1974) at age 25-26.
early_history_summary: Born Nirmala Nagpal in Bombay to parents who migrated from Pakistan after Partition. Family was extremely poor. She started working as a child artist at age 3, became a background dancer at 10, and was taken under choreographer B. Sohanlal's wing at 13, becoming his assistant and choreographing her first song at 14.
family_context_summary: Parents migrated from Pakistan after Partition; father was previously wealthy but lost everything. Family was extremely poor; father later developed cancer. She became the primary earner at age 3.
primary_early_advantage_tags: child labor, poverty, Bollywood immersion, mentorship, early specialization
evidence_summary: Saroj Khan was born to a family that fled Pakistan after Partition and fell into extreme poverty. She began working in Bollywood at age 3 as a child artist to support her family. At 13, she became assistant to choreographer B. Sohanlal, and choreographed her first song at 14. Her entire childhood was spent immersed in the Hindi film industry, giving her unparalleled domain exposure. The adversity of poverty and displacement catalyzed her early entry into the profession.
starting_point: Born to a family that fled Pakistan after Partition and fell into extreme poverty in Bombay; father was previously wealthy but lost everything.
current_position: Died on 3 July 2020 at age 71 in Mumbai; final status: Bollywood's most celebrated choreographer with a record 8 Filmfare Awards and 4 National Film Awards.

trajectory.event: Began working as a child artist in the film Nazarana to support her impoverished family.
Appeared as a background dancer in Howrah Bridge.
Choreographed her first Bollywood song, 'Nigahein Milane Ko Jee Chahta Hai' from Dil Hi Toh Hai.
First independent choreographer credit for the film Geeta Mera Naam.
Choreographed the iconic 'Ek Do Teen' from Tezaab, launching her to widespread acclaim.
Choreographed 'Dola Re Dola' in Devdas, winning a National Film Award.
Died of cardiac arrest in Mumbai.

name: Primož Roglič
milestone_by_age_26: Won gold in the team event at the 2007 FIS Nordic Junior World Ski Championships and two Continental Cup victories at age 17; later won his first WorldTour cycling stage at the 2016 Giro d'Italia at age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Trbovlje, Slovenia, Roglič pursued ski jumping from age 10, practicing at a local jump near his childhood home. By 13, he competed in his first FIS competition. At 17, he won Junior World Championship gold (team) and two Continental Cup events. After a crash and stalled progression, he retired from ski jumping in 2012 and switched to cycling.
family_context_summary: Born in Trbovlje, Slovenia (then part of Yugoslavia). Father was a former miner who worked at a local water purification plant; mother was a housewife. Only child, grew up in the small mining village of Kisovec.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Slovenian ski jumping culture, early specialization, athletic transferability, Planica
evidence_summary: Primož Roglič grew up in Kisovec, a small mining village in Slovenia, where ski jumping was the dominant sport. He started jumping at age 10 and joined the Slovenian national pipeline, winning Junior World Championship gold (team) and two Continental Cup events at 17. His father was a former miner; the family was working-class. After his ski jumping career stalled, he switched to cycling at 23, transferring his athletic conditioning to become one of the world's top cyclists.
starting_point: Born in Trbovlje, Slovenia to a working-class family; father a former miner working at a water purification plant, mother a housewife; only child raised in the small mining village of Kisovec.
current_position: Professional cyclist for Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe; multiple Grand Tour winner (Vuelta a Espana 2019, 2020, 2021; Giro d'Italia 2023); one of the most successful cyclists of his generation.

trajectory.event: Participated in first FIS ski jumping competition in Villach, Austria.
Won gold in team event at Junior World Ski Championships and two Continental Cup victories.
Retired from ski jumping after stalled progression; began exploring cycling through duathlon.
Took first WorldTour win with individual time trial stage at the Giro d'Italia.
Won first Grand Tour, the Vuelta a Espana.
Won second consecutive Vuelta a Espana; finished 2nd at Tour de France.
Won the Giro d'Italia, his fourth Grand Tour victory.

name: Tim Bevan
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Working Title Films in London with Sarah Radclyffe in 1983 at age 25, establishing what would become one of the most successful British production companies.
early_history_summary: Born in Queenstown, New Zealand, Bevan was educated at Sidcot School (a Quaker boarding school) and Cheltenham College. He started his career as a production runner on the soap opera Close to Home, then worked at New Zealand's National Film Unit. In the early 1980s he moved to Britain, worked at Video Arts (John Cleese's company), and in 1983 co-founded Working Title Films.
family_context_summary: Born in Queenstown, New Zealand. Educated at Sidcot School, a Quaker boarding independent school in Somerset, and Cheltenham College, a boarding independent school in Gloucestershire. This suggests an upper-middle-class family with means for private education.
primary_early_advantage_tags: boarding school education, British film industry, co-founder partnership, London
evidence_summary: Tim Bevan was born in New Zealand and educated at elite British boarding schools (Sidcot and Cheltenham College), suggesting family means. He began his career as a production runner in New Zealand before moving to London in the early 1980s. At 25, he co-founded Working Title Films with Sarah Radclyffe, leveraging his film industry experience and British network. The company would go on to produce some of the most successful British films.
starting_point: Born in Queenstown, New Zealand; educated at elite British boarding schools (Sidcot and Cheltenham College), suggesting an upper-middle-class family with means for private education.
current_position: Co-chairman of Working Title Films; films have grossed almost $7 billion worldwide and won 12 Academy Awards; appointed CBE.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Working Title Films in London with Sarah Radclyffe.
Produced My Beautiful Laundrette, a landmark British independent film.
Produced Four Weddings and a Funeral, a major international hit.
Produced Elizabeth, sharing a BAFTA award for Best British Film.
Produced Les Miserables, nominated for Best Picture at the Academy Awards.
Produced The Substance, a critical and commercial success.

name: Satoshi Ōmura
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; had a B.S. from University of Yamanashi (1958) and was pursuing his M.S. at Tokyo University of Science (completed 1963). Fame arrived with the discovery of ivermectin in 1978 and the Nobel Prize in 2015.
early_history_summary: Born into a farming family in Nirasaki, Yamanashi, Japan. Excelled at sports, particularly cross-country skiing, reaching national representative levels. Graduated with a B.S. from University of Yamanashi in 1958, then worked as a high school teacher before pursuing his M.S. at Tokyo University of Science.
family_context_summary: Born into a farming household in Nirasaki, Yamanashi, Japan. Father was a proactive leading member of his village; mother was an elementary school teacher and gifted piano player.
evidence_summary: Satoshi Omura was born into a farming family in Yamanashi, Japan. He graduated with a B.S. from the University of Yamanashi in 1958 and worked as a high school teacher before pursuing his M.S. at Tokyo University of Science (completed 1963). His PhD came in 1968 at age 33, and his landmark discovery of ivermectin came in 1978 at age 43. He won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2015. No material career milestone occurred by age 26.

name: Imre Bujdosó
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship gold in team sabre at the 1982 World Fencing Championships in Rome at age 23, and won a junior world championship medal in 1979 at age 20.
early_history_summary: Born in Berrettyóújfalu, Hungary, moved to Budapest at age 1. Started fencing at BSE in 1973 at age 14 under coach Tolnay Kornél. Won national youth champion in 1974 at age 15, and a junior world championship medal in 1979 at age 20. Joined the Hungarian national team in 1982.
family_context_summary: Born in Berrettyóújfalu, Hungary. Family moved to Budapest when he was one year old. Not much else documented about family background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Hungarian fencing tradition, national team, early specialization, team sport
evidence_summary: Imre Bujdosó was born in Hungary and started fencing at age 14 under coach Tolnay Kornél at BSE in Budapest. Hungary's deep fencing tradition and elite pipeline provided the ecosystem for his development. He won national youth champion at 15, a junior world championship medal at 20, and World Championship gold in team sabre at 23. The Hungarian national team system and club structure (BSE, later Vasas SC) concentrated opportunity.
starting_point: Born in Berrettyóújfalu, Hungary; family moved to Budapest at age one; family background otherwise not documented.
current_position: Fencing coach; moved back to Hungary in 2025 to coach in Torokbalint after 30 years coaching in Koblenz, Germany.

trajectory.event: Won national youth championship in sabre fencing.
Won junior world championship medal in sabre.
Won World Championship gold in team sabre at Rome; joined Hungarian national team.
Won Olympic gold in team sabre at the Seoul Olympics.
Won World Championship gold (team) and European Championship gold (team).
Won Olympic silver in team sabre at Barcelona.
Retired from competitive fencing; moved to Germany to coach at the Olympic Center in Koblenz.

name: Vandana Shiva
milestone_by_age_26: Completed PhD in philosophy at the University of Western Ontario in 1978 at age 25-26, but her environmental activism career began after age 26; fame arrived with founding RFSTN in 1982 and the Right Livelihood Award in 1993.
early_history_summary: Born in Dehradun, India. Father was a conservator of forests; mother was a farmer with a love for nature. Studied physics at Panjab University (B.S. 1972), then philosophy of science at University of Guelph (M.S. 1977) and University of Western Ontario (PhD 1978).
family_context_summary: Born in Dehradun, India. Father was a conservator of forests; mother was a farmer with a love for nature and a committed Gandhian. Parents were feminists who encouraged independence.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a conservator of forests and mother was a farmer, providing early exposure to environmental and ecological concerns, though not directly to activism as a career.
evidence_summary: Vandana Shiva was born in Dehradun, India, to a forest conservator father and farmer mother. She earned a B.S. in physics (1972), an M.S. in philosophy of science (1977), and a PhD in philosophy (1978) at age 25-26. While she participated as a volunteer in the Chipko movement during university breaks, her environmental activism career began after age 26 with the founding of RFSTN in 1982. Her fame as an activist came well after age 26.

name: Knut Knudsen
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in the 4000m individual pursuit at the 1972 Munich Olympics at age 22, and World Championship gold in the same discipline in 1973 at age 23.
early_history_summary: Born in Levanger, Norway. From Nord-Trondelag, near the Arctic Circle. Competed in the 1968 Olympics at age 17, placing 5th in the individual pursuit. Won Olympic gold in 1972 and World Championship gold in 1973.
family_context_summary: Born in Levanger, Norway. From Nord-Trondelag, near the Arctic Circle. Not much documented about family background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early Olympic competition, physical talent, Norwegian cycling, harsh training conditions
evidence_summary: Knut Knudsen was born in Levanger, Norway, near the Arctic Circle, where winter temperatures reached -30C. He competed in the 1968 Olympics at age 17, placing 5th in the individual pursuit, demonstrating exceptional early talent. By 22, he won Olympic gold in the same event, and by 23, World Championship gold. Little is documented about his family background or early coaching.
starting_point: Born in Levanger, Norway, near the Arctic Circle; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from professional cycling; living in Norway. Voted best time trialist in the world during 1979-1981 period.

trajectory.event: Competed in the Mexico City Olympics, placing 5th in the 4000m individual pursuit.
Won Olympic gold in the 4000m individual pursuit at the Munich Olympics.
Won World Championship gold in the individual pursuit (amateurs); won Norwegian National Road Race Championships.
Turned professional; won first Giro d'Italia stage.
Won Tirreno-Adriatico overall classification.
Won GP Eddy Merckx and two Giro d'Italia stages; voted best time trialist in the world.

name: Didier Dinart
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship gold with the French national handball team in 2001 at age 24, and made his national team debut in December 1996 at age 19.
early_history_summary: Born in Pointe-a-Pitre, Guadeloupe. Started playing handball at 13. At 16, he moved to mainland France to join Dijon's handball program, leaving his mother behind. After three seasons at Dijon, he joined Montpellier HB. Made his French national team debut in December 1996 at age 19.
family_context_summary: Born and raised by his mother in Pointe-a-Pitre, Guadeloupe. She could not afford sports and studies tuition; his move to France was funded by the Dijon club. He grew up as an angry child in Guadeloupe.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Guadeloupe displacement, poverty, handball pipeline, defensive specialization, physical size
evidence_summary: Didier Dinart was born in Pointe-a-Pitre, Guadeloupe, and raised by his mother in poverty. At 16, he left his island and family to join Dijon's handball program in mainland France, with his tuition funded by the club. He channeled childhood anger into defensive specialization, becoming the 'general of the France defence.' By 19, he debuted for the French national team, and by 24, he won World Championship gold. His journey from a small Caribbean island to Olympic glory exemplifies constraint-driven self-creation.
starting_point: Born and raised by his mother in Pointe-a-Pitre, Guadeloupe; grew up in poverty, mother could not afford sports tuition.
current_position: Coach of US Ivry Handball and the Montenegro national team; former head coach of the French national team (2016-2021).

trajectory.event: Left Guadeloupe to join Dijon handball program in mainland France.
Made debut for the French national team on 20 December 1996 against Croatia.
Won first World Championship gold with France.
Won EHF Champions League with Montpellier HB.
Won Olympic gold at the Beijing Olympics.
Won second consecutive Olympic gold at the London Olympics.
As head coach, led France to World Championship gold.

name: Sante Gaiardoni
milestone_by_age_26: Won two gold medals at the 1960 Rome Olympics in the 1000m time trial and 1000m sprint at age 21, becoming the first man to win the kilometre/sprint double; also won World Championship gold in the sprint the same year.
early_history_summary: Born in Villafranca di Verona, Italy, to humble origins. Grew up working in fields, developing powerful legs. Discovered by semiprofessional cyclist Arnaldo Faccioli, who invited him to train. Won the Italian title in 1957 at age 17-18, and World Championship silver medals in 1958 and 1959.
family_context_summary: Born in Villafranca di Verona, Italy, to humble origins. Grew up working in the fields, developing physical strength. Could not afford a bicycle initially; promised to pay for one with prize money from his first race.
primary_early_advantage_tags: humble origins, physical labor, Italian cycling, mentor discovery, track sprint talent
evidence_summary: Sante Gaiardoni was born in Villafranca di Verona to humble origins, growing up working in fields where his legs became powerful and explosive. He was discovered by semiprofessional cyclist Arnaldo Faccioli, who trained him despite Gaiardoni's inability to afford a bicycle. The Italian cycling federation noticed his exceptional power, directing him to track racing. By 17, he won the Italian title; by 19-20, World Championship silver medals; and at 21, two Olympic golds at the 1960 Rome Games.
starting_point: Born in Villafranca di Verona, Italy to humble origins; grew up working in fields, could not afford a bicycle initially.
current_position: Died on 30 November 2023 at age 84 in Motta Visconti, Italy; final role: retired cyclist and bicycle shop owner in Milan.

trajectory.event: Won the Italian national sprint title.
Won World Championship silver medal in sprint (amateurs).
Won two Olympic gold medals at the Rome Olympics (1000m time trial and sprint) and World Championship gold in sprint.
Won World Championship gold in sprint as a professional at Rocourt, Belgium.
Won Italian national sprint title, ending Antonio Maspes's five-year reign.
Retired from professional cycling; ran a bicycle shop in Milan.
Died in Motta Visconti, Italy.

name: Hongman Choi
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2003 Ssireum Championship (Korean traditional wrestling) at age 22-23, and the K-1 Seoul Grand Prix in 2005 at age 24-25.
early_history_summary: Born in Jeju City, South Korea. Exceptional physical stature from a young age (2.18m, 160kg+). Joined the Ssireum club at Dong-A University because they offered good food. Graduated in 2002 and joined the LG Investment & Securities Ssireum team. Won the Ssireum Championship in 2003, then transitioned to K-1 kickboxing in 2005.
family_context_summary: Born in Jeju City, South Korea. Not much documented about family background. Exceptional physical stature from a young age.
primary_early_advantage_tags: extraordinary physical size, Ssireum, K-1, Korean combat sports
evidence_summary: Hongman Choi was born in Jeju City, South Korea, with extraordinary physical stature (2.18m, 160kg+) that defined his combat sports career. He joined the Ssireum club at Dong-A University, attracted by the promise of food, and won the Ssireum Championship in 2003. His physical size was the primary leverage, enabling a transition to K-1 kickboxing where he won the 2005 Seoul Grand Prix. Little is documented about his family background.
starting_point: Born in Jeju City, South Korea; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Largely retired from top-level combat sports; made occasional appearances in Road FC and professional wrestling.
